source.author: Jean Michel Sellier
source.title: On a quantum inspired approach to train machine learning models
checked_locations: Section 4.5, best-solution recording step, PDF page 10

formal_scope: Pointwise complex algebra and a mathematical model of best-observed-loss recording, not PDE solution theory or an implementation audit.

schrodinger_split.meaning: Equivalent real/imaginary component equations, retaining h on the left-hand side.
schrodinger_split.assumptions: All scalar inputs and potential are real. Complex component values and derivatives are supplied pointwise. Physically m>0; algebraic equivalence also holds for the totalized division convention of real fields.

schrodinger_derivatives.assumptions: The same pointwise setup, with h nonzero.

printed_eq9_counterexample.meaning: With h=m=1, U=0, R=I=dtR=dxxI=0, dtI=-1, dxxR=2, the printed system holds but the complex equation fails.
printed_eq9_counterexample.scope: Algebraic counterexample to the claimed component equivalence, not a counterexample to the full training algorithm or a supplied PDE solution.

best_loss_antitone.meaning: A running minimum of observed real scores never increases.
best_loss_antitone.assumptions: The recorder is modeled by b0=loss0 and b(n+1)=min(bn,loss(n+1)). No candidate generator is modeled.

best_loss_attained.meaning: The recorded score belongs to a candidate evaluated at or before the current step.
best_loss_attained.assumptions: The same running-minimum model. A fixed comparable evaluation criterion is needed to interpret scores as progress on one objective.

finding_status: Printed equation (9) is algebraically inconsistent with (7)-(8) under the transcribed conventions; the intended implementation and any author clarification are unverified.
